patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Recently started college. History of polysubstance abuse.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and manage a young adult patient presenting with altered mental status, suspected of having a serious drug reaction.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I—can’t… talk right now. I’m very sleepy and not feeling well. My temperature is extremely high, and my body feels stiff.
Have you started any new medications in the past week—particularly antidepressants like fluoxetine or sertraline, antipsychotics, or have you had any surgery with general anesthesia recently?
I can’t answer right now—I’m too sleepy. I don’t know about any new medicines or surgeries, but I’ve had a lot of drug use recently. My temperature is very high and my muscles feel rigid.
What specific drugs or substances did you use most recently?
I can’t… cooperate—I'm too drowsy. I’ve used a lot of different drugs recently, and I feel very hot with stiff muscles.
Did these symptoms come on suddenly within the past few hours, or have they been developing gradually over several days?
“Doctor, I think this came on suddenly—within a few hours—after I was out in very hot weather.” “I became extremely sleepy and then started to feel very hot with stiff, rigid muscles.”
Are your muscles showing any rhythmic jerking or twitching movements, or are they continuously stiff without twitching?

Doctor: Are your muscles showing any rhythmic jerking or twitching movements, or are they continuously stiff without twitching? Patient: They’re continuously stiff—no rhythmic jerking that I notice, just very rigid and unwell.
Are you sweating profusely right now, or is your skin dry and hot to the touch?

Doctor: Are you sweating profusely right now, or is your skin dry and hot to the touch? Patient: My skin feels very hot, and my mouth and lips are dry—I don’t think I’m sweating much. I’m extremely sleepy and my muscles stay stiff.

Doctor, I can’t really cooperate or speak clearly—I’m very drowsy and can barely respond. My skin feels extremely hot with dry mouth and lips, and my muscles are rigid all the time. I think this started within a few hours after being in very hot weather and using substances.
Were the drugs you used stimulants like cocaine or methamphetamine, hallucinogens, or have you taken any medications for mental health conditions like schizophrenia or depression?

“I don’t remember exactly which drugs—I’ve used a lot of different substances recently. I can’t say whether they were stimulants or mental-health meds, but I’m very hot with dry mouth and continuously stiff muscles, and I can barely stay awake.”
Do you feel like your heart is racing, or have you noticed if your blood pressure seems high or low (feeling faint when standing)?
“I can’t really stand or feel faint right now—I’m too drowsy. I think my heart is racing and I feel like my blood pressure is high, but I’m not sure because I can barely respond.”

Doctor: I need you to cooperate—are you having trouble breathing, and do you have any nausea or confusion right now? Patient: I’m too drowsy to answer properly; I feel extremely unwell, my body is rigid, and I can’t really think clearly. Doctor: Do you have any sweating at all, or is it dry and hot like before? Patient: It’s dry and very hot—I don’t think I’m sweating much.

Doctor: I’m going to examine you—stay as still as you can. Can you tell me if your muscles are stiff all over, and whether you’re confused even briefly when you wake up? Patient: Yes… my muscles feel stiff everywhere, not twitching—just rigid. I can’t think clearly and I’m too sleepy to really understand what’s happening.
Have you recently started or increased any medication for depression, anxiety, or schizophrenia, or have you stopped taking any medication for Parkinson's disease?

I can’t really cooperate—I’m too drowsy. I don’t know about any new depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, or Parkinson’s meds, but I’ve been using a lot of different drugs recently. My body feels extremely hot with dry mouth and continuously stiff muscles, and I’m barely able to respond.

“Doctor, I can’t really cooperate or speak much—I’m extremely sleepy. My skin feels very hot and dry, and my muscles are continuously rigid without twitching. I was out in very hot weather and used a lot of substances shortly before this started.”

Doctor: Now please continue your dialogue. Patient: I’m sorry—I can’t cooperate much. My skin is very hot and dry, my mouth is dry, and my muscles feel continuously rigid; I’m also extremely sleepy and not really thinking clearly.
[DDX] Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome, Heat Stroke (Classic), Serotonin Syndrome, Sympathomimetic Toxicity, Malignant Hyperthermia
